scope: All nine ordered pairs over {t,g+,g-} for one nondegenerate two-carbon chain under pure translation T=(0,0,c). This is not an enumeration of longer-period, helical, defective or disordered chains.

proof: Two-carbon pure-translation periodicity makes consecutive carbon positions A, B, A+T, B+T, A+2T, ... . Set v=B-A and w=T-v.

Consecutive bond vectors are v,w,v,w,... . The normals for the first dihedral are v cross w and w cross v = -(v cross w); the next dihedral has the same opposite-normal relation. If v cross w != 0, both dihedrals are trans, 180 degrees modulo 360.

Equal C-C bond lengths give |v|^2=|T-v|^2, hence v dot T=|T|^2/2. For |T|=c and bond length l, each bond has axial projection c/2 and transverse magnitude sqrt(l^2-c^2/4). Here l>c/2, so the chain is noncollinear and the dihedrals are defined.
A gauche request is rejected by this analytic necessary closure condition. No failed numerical builder or optimization is asserted.

geometric_check.constructed_from: Chemical bond length, cell translation, arbitrary setting angle 35 degrees; no coordinate template

symmetry.mirror_argument: The operation (x,y,1/2-z) fixes the transverse coordinates. The two carbons on a nonzero-width zigzag have distinct transverse positions. Thus each carbon lies on a mirror plane: z=1/4 or 3/4 modulo 1. This imposes no condition on its x,y coordinates and therefore no condition on the in-plane setting angle.
symmetry.axis_argument: The operation G:(x,y,z)->(x+1/2,1/2-y,z) exchanges the two chain axes, so Baxis=(X+1/2,1/2-Y). The screw S:(x,y,z)->(-x,-y,z+1/2) cannot exchange these two axes, because its y equation would require -Y=1/2-Y modulo 1. It therefore fixes each axis, requiring 2X=2Y=0 modulo 1.
symmetry.atomic_sites: Each initial C/H independent atom is on a 4c mirror site (x,y,1/4); x and y are free. Fixed chain axes must not be misdescribed as fixed atomic coordinates.
symmetry.setting_angle: Continuous angle of the whole trans zigzag plane around c; the second chain is symmetry related. It is not a C-C-C-C torsion.
symmetry.general_origin_change_rule: For f'=f+delta, keep the same physical structure by transforming each translation to t'=t+(I-R)delta modulo integers. An arbitrary origin change is a gauge choice, not an independent packing or axial-slide degree of freedom.
